question.text:
Given $\operatorname{Instant}(i)$ : $i$ is an instant in time" and Precedes( $x, y$ ): " $x$ precedes $y$ ", which of the following correctly expresses "time has a beginning" - i.e., there exists a first instant that is not preceded by any other instant?

  1. $\exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge \forall y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \rightarrow \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y)))$
  2. $\exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge \neg \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(y, x)))$
  3. $\forall x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \rightarrow \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(y, x)))$
  4. $\exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(y, x)))$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Given $\operatorname{Instant}(i)$ : " $i$ is an instant in time" and Precedes $(x, y)$ : " $x$ precedes $y$ ", which of the following correctly expresses "time has no end" - i.e., every instant is followed by another instant?

  1. $\exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge \forall y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \rightarrow \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y)))$
  2. $\neg \exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge \neg \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y)))$
  3. $\forall x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \rightarrow \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge$ Precedes $(x, y)))$
  4. $\forall x \forall y(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge \operatorname{Instant}(y) \rightarrow \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y))$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Given Instant $(i)$ : " $i$ is an instant in time" and Precedes $(x, y)$ : " $x$ precedes $y$ ", which of the following correctly expresses the combined statement "time has a beginning but has no end"?

  1. $\exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge eg \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge$ Precedes $(y, x))) \wedge \exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge eg \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y)))$
  2. $\exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge eg \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(y, x))) \wedge orall x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) ightarrow \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y)))$
  3. $ orall x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) ightarrow \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge$ Precedes $(y, x))) \wedge orall x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) ightarrow \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y)))$
  4. (D) $\exists x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) \wedge eg \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge$ Precedes $(y, x))) \wedge eg orall x(\operatorname{Instant}(x) ightarrow \exists y(\operatorname{Instant}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Precedes}(x, y)))$

question.text:
Given Person $(x)$ : " $x$ is a person" and Ruler $(x)$ : " $x$ is a ruler", which of the following correctly expresses "exactly one person is a ruler" in first-order logic?

  1. $\forall x \forall y((\operatorname{Person}(x) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(x) \wedge \operatorname{Person}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(y)) \rightarrow(x=y))$
  2. $\exists x(\operatorname{Person}(x) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(x))$
  3. $\exists x(\operatorname{Person}(x) \wedge$ Ruler $(x)) \wedge \forall x \forall y((\operatorname{Person}(x) \wedge$ Ruler $(x) \wedge \operatorname{Person}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(y)) \rightarrow(x=y))$
  4. $\exists x \forall y((\operatorname{Person}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(y)) \leftrightarrow(x=y))$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Given Person $(x)$ : " $x$ is a person" and Ruler $(x)$ : " $x$ is a ruler", which of the following correctly expresses "at most one person is a ruler" in first-order logic?

  1. $\exists x(\operatorname{Person}(x) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(x))$
  2. $\forall x \forall y((\operatorname{Person}(x) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(x) \wedge \operatorname{Person}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(y)) \rightarrow(x=y))$
  3. $\exists x \forall y((\operatorname{Person}(y) \wedge \operatorname{Ruler}(y)) \rightarrow(x=y))$
  4. $\forall x(\operatorname{Person}(x) \rightarrow \neg \operatorname{Ruler}(x))$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic
